title: Celebration Music and Dance
strapline: Music from many celebrations, ribbons in both hands, and a room with the furniture pushed back.
intent: Children explore rhythm and movement while meeting the music of several cultural celebrations.
Moving to an unfamiliar rhythm builds coordination and whole-body control.
Children hear that celebration sounds different in different families, and that all of it is music.
Ribbons and scarves make the beat visible, which helps children who cannot yet feel it.
Joining in with a group dance builds confidence and belonging.
implementation: Play a genuine range of celebration music — dance music from Diwali, carols, songs from Hanukkah.
Provide ribbons and scarves so every child has something to move with.
Clear a real space; this needs room to move, not a corner of the carpet.
Model clapping and moving with the beat, then follow the children's inventions.
Name the instruments children can hear — drum, bell, shaker, voice.
Let children lead a section each: everyone copies their move.
Invite families to suggest or send music their own family celebrates with.
key_questions: Can you hear the beat? Can you clap it with me?
What instrument do you think is making that sound?
How does this music make you want to move?
Is this music fast or slow, loud or quiet?
What music does your family play at a special time?

impact.text: Children move, play and perform with growing confidence in front of others.
Children experiment with rhythm, volume and their own variations.
Children develop coordination and control moving through space.
Children learn that families, faiths and ways of celebrating vary, and that is interesting.
Children join in and contribute an idea to a whole-group activity.
Children pick up new vocabulary for instruments and sounds.

enhancements: A permanent instrument trolley children can reach without asking.
A recording of the children's own celebration band played back to them.
A parent or family member invited in to play or dance with the children.
A slow-and-fast game where the music changes and bodies must follow.
A scarf-and-light session combining the ribbons with torches in a dim room.
A class playlist built from the music families send in.

playing_exploring: Children move however the music takes them, with no right answer.
Ribbons and scarves invite open, whole-body experimentation.
active_learning: Children keep going through a whole piece and return to favourite moves.
Leading a move for the group takes courage and they build it.
creating_thinking: Children invent movements and adapt them as the music changes.
They notice and describe differences between one celebration's music and another.
